Debugger, sound and CD-ROM tools, a C++ template, real-hardware upload, and a better play page.

- **Debugging** (`debug`, `profile`): breakpoints and watchpoints that halt the CPU
  mid-frame, with disassembly, call stack, registers and single-stepping; a
  per-function CPU profiler. Frame numbers stay deterministic.
- **Sound and CD-ROM** (`spu`, `cd_log`): every SPU voice as text and samples to
  `.wav`; a log of CD-ROM commands and sector reads named by disc file. `check`
  now also reports CD-ROM drive errors.
- **Toolchain**: float/double work on the PS1 with Ubuntu's MIPS toolchain (a MIPS I
  compiler runtime replaces its hard-float libgcc helpers); a C++ template
  (`psn00bsdk-cpp`) that passes the C template's goldens.
- **Discs and hardware**: `disc` makes a bootable `.cue`/`.bin` from an EXE or ELF;
  `send_to_console` uploads an EXE to a real PS1 running Unirom (`nops`).
- **Play page**: drag and drop, a memory-card panel (export/import/format, saves
  listed with icons), a PlayStation touch pad on phones, installable and offline.
- **Builds and CI**: reproducible core builds (CI fails if `data/cores` doesn't match
  `core/`); Windows and macOS in the test matrix; a Vercel deployment smoke test;
  optional npm publishing (`npx ps1-test-mcp`) with an `NPM_TOKEN` secret.
